accepted.question_text: For nonlinear elastostatics, prove that the elastic energy admits minimizers when the stored-energy function W is quasiconvex and satisfies the singular determinant condition W(A) tends to infinity as det A tends to 0 from above, with W(A) infinite when det A is nonpositive so that orientation collapse is excluded.

evidence.quote: W (A) → ∞ as det A → 0 + .
Problem 1. Prove the existence of energy minimizers for elastostatics for quasiconvex stored-energy functions satisfying (2.7).

accepted.question_text: Find practical criteria or methods for verifying polyconvexity and quasiconvexity for useful anisotropic stored-energy functions in nonlinear elasticity, especially beyond isotropic materials where the singular-value representation W(A)=Φ(v1,v2,v3) is available.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Are there ways of verifying polyconvexity and quasiconvexity for a useful class of anisotropic stored-energy functions?

accepted.question_text: Determine conditions under which a global minimizer y* of the nonlinear elastic energy I(y)=∫Ω W(Dy) dx is smooth in Ω and smooth up to the boundary, apart from expected singularities near points where the displacement and traction boundary parts meet.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. When is the minimizer y∗ in Theorem 2.1 smooth?
Here smooth means C ∞ in Ω, and C ∞ up to the boundary

accepted.question_text: Can the Lavrentiev phenomenon occur in elastostatics under growth assumptions on the stored-energy function that force every finite-energy deformation to be continuous, including for mixed boundary conditions or interior singularities?

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Can the Lavrentiev phenomenon occur for elastostatics under growth conditions on the stored-energy function ensuring that all finite-energy deformations are continuous?
Whether such examples can be constructed for mixed boundary conditions of the type (2.1), even in two dimensions, or be associated with singularities in the interior of Ω, remains open.

accepted.question_text: Under reasonable growth conditions on the stored-energy function W, determine whether global minimizers or suitably defined local minimizers of I(y)=∫Ω W(Dy) dx satisfy the weak Euler-Lagrange equation ∫Ω DAW(Dy) · Dφ dx = 0 for all smooth test fields φ that vanish on the displacement boundary.

evidence.quote: we obtain the weak form of the Euler-Lagrange equation for I
Problem 5. Prove or disprove that, under reasonable growth conditions on W, global or suitably defined local minimizers of I satisfy the weak form (2.4) of the Euler-Lagrange equation.

accepted.question_text: Under reasonable growth conditions on W, determine whether global minimizers or suitably defined local minimizers y* of the elastic energy satisfy uniform positivity of the Jacobian determinant, namely whether there exists ε>0 such that det Dy*(x) ≥ ε for almost every x in Ω.

evidence.quote: det Dy∗ (x) ≥ ε for a.e. x ∈ Ω
Problem 6. Prove or disprove that, under reasonable growth conditions on W, global or suitably defined local minimizers of I satisfy (2.19).

accepted.question_text: Justify the Ciarlet-Necas constrained minimization formulation, or an appropriate modification of it, as a model of smooth frictionless self-contact for elastic bodies, including the vanishing of tangential stress components near self-contact and the regularity of the free boundary.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Justify the Ciarlet-Nečas minimization problem, or an appropriate modification of it, as a model of smooth self-contact.
The problem here is to construct suitable variations in the neighbourhood of a region of self-contact of a minimizer

accepted.question_text: For a homogeneous elastic body with pure displacement boundary conditions, strictly polyconvex stored-energy function W, and reference domain Ω homeomorphic to a ball, prove or disprove uniqueness of sufficiently smooth equilibrium solutions.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Prove or disprove the uniqueness of sufficiently smooth equilibrium solutions to pure displacement boundary-value problems for homogeneous bodies when the stored-energy function W is strictly polyconvex and Ω is homeomorphic to a ball.

accepted.question_text: Develop general methods for proving the existence of local minimizers of the elastic energy I that are not global minimizers, and for proving the existence of other weak solutions of the equilibrium equations, including equilibrium solutions that are not local minimizers.

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Devise general methods for proving the existence of local minimizers of I that are not global minimizers, and of other weak solutions of the equilibrium equations.
How can one prove the existence of equilibrium solutions that are not local minimizers?

accepted.question_text: Develop local and global bifurcation theories for nonlinear elastostatics that apply to mixed displacement-traction boundary conditions, such as three-dimensional buckling problems where the displacement and traction boundary portions meet.

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Develop local and global bifurcation theories for nonlinear elastostatics that apply to mixed displacement-traction boundary conditions.
there is a different approach to be discovered that circumvents this difficulty.

accepted.question_text: Clarify how variational fracture models with energy I(y)=∫Ω W(Dy) dx plus a surface term over the jump set Sy relate to classical fracture mechanics and to nonlinear elastostatics, especially for fracture initiation, stability, and local minimizers.

evidence.quote: A generalization of the energy functional (2.2) to deformations allowing for fracture is
Problem 11. Clarify the status of models based on the energy functional (2.31) with respect to classical fracture mechanics and to nonlinear elastostatics.

accepted.question_text: Prove global existence and uniqueness for initial-boundary value problems in properly formulated dynamic theories of nonlinear elasticity, including isothermal thermoelastic or thermoviscoelastic equations with appropriate boundary and initial data.

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Prove the global existence and uniqueness of solutions to initialboundary value problems for properly formulated dynamic theories of nonlinear elasticity.
These equations need to be supplemented by boundary conditions such as (2.1), (2.6) and by the initial conditions

accepted.question_text: Develop a qualitative dynamics for dynamic elasticity theories: after obtaining a global solution theory, determine convergence to equilibria, attraction basins, stable and unstable manifolds, global attractors, and whether dynamic orbits realize local minimizing sequences for ballistic free energy.

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Develop a qualitative dynamics for dynamic theories of elasticity.
the points at issue are the usual ones for dissipative dynamical systems

accepted.question_text: Develop criteria for dynamic stability and instability of equilibria in nonlinear elasticity, including which notions of local minimizer ensure Lyapunov or asymptotic stability and how instability can be justified.

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Develop criteria for the dynamic stability and instability of equilibria.
it is not clear which kinds of local minimizers are needed to ensure dynamical stability.

accepted.question_text: Establish the relationship between continuum elasticity theory and atomistic models, including whether elasticity can be derived from quantum, density-functional, Thomas-Fermi, or interatomic-potential models; what limiting energy and function space arise from atomistic minimizers; and how atomistic-continuum matching methods such as quasicontinuum schemes can be rigorously understood.

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Establish the status of elasticity theory with respect to atomistic models.
The second approach is to consider the true minimizers of the discrete problems, and to try to understand what functional their limit minimizes.
A rigorous understanding of such methods is lacking.

accepted.question_text: For materials undergoing phase transformations with fine microstructure, explain why fine microstructure forms, predict its morphology, and determine the material properties at macroscopic scales much larger than the microstructure scale, ideally within a suitably formulated dynamical theory that accounts for interface kinetics.

evidence.quote: Why does fine microstructure form? To what extent can we predict its morphology? What are the properties of the material at a macroscale much larger than the microscale of the microstructure?
it is neither clear what such a theory should be

accepted.question_text: For a thermoelastic single crystal undergoing a diffusionless phase transformation at critical temperature θc, determine the quasiconvexification K(θ)^qc of the set K(θ) of energy-minimizing deformation gradients for temperatures θ≤θc, including the cubic-to-tetragonal case at and below θc.

evidence.quote: K(θ) = {A ∈ M+ 3×3 : ψ(A, θ) = 0} be the set of energy-minimizing deformation gradients.
where for a compact set K ⊂ M 3×3 , K qc denotes the quasiconvexification of K.
Problem 16. Determine K(θ)qc for θ ≤ θc .

accepted.question_text: For free-energy functions ψ(A,θ) of elastic crystals, characterize the displacement boundary portions ∂Ω1 and boundary data g for which the minimum of Iθ(y)=∫Ω ψ(Dy,θ) dx over deformations y with y|∂Ω1=g is attained, and characterize those for which it is not; in particular, determine whether non-attainment associated with microstructure is generic or exceptional.

evidence.quote: Problem 17. For free-energy functions ψ(A, θ) of elastic crystals, determine for which ∂Ω1 ⊂ ∂Ω and g : ∂Ω1 → R3 the minimum of Iθ (y) = ψ(Dy, θ) dx in A = {y ∈ W 1,1 (Ω; R3 ) : y|∂Ω1 = g} is attained, and for which it is not.
For example, is non-attainment generic or exceptional?

accepted.question_text: Give rigorous derivations of one-dimensional rod models and two-dimensional plate or shell models from three-dimensional elasticity, proving that their solutions approximate appropriate three-dimensional elastic solutions as the thickness parameter h tends to zero, with convergence and error estimates that handle loads, boundary conditions, buckling, and boundary layers.

evidence.quote: Problem 18. Give a rigorous derivation of models of rods, plates and shells, showing that their solutions well approximate appropriate solutions to three-dimensional elasticity for small values of the thickness parameter h.
one would ideally like results showing that the solution sets for boundary-value value problems of three-dimensional elasticity converge as h → 0
